name: Macrodactyly of Fingers

criteria.description: Progressive enlargement of one or more fingers involving soft tissue and bone
Asymmetric overgrowth of affected digit(s) compared to contralateral side
Radiographic evidence of osseous hypertrophy and soft tissue proliferation
No evidence of systemic syndromes or generalized overgrowth disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive localized digit enlargement with radiologic confirmation of osseous and soft tissue overgrowth in absence of systemic syndromes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may be considered to exclude syndromic causes.

occasional.symptomName: Entrapment neuropathy of the ulnar nerve at elbow

imaging: X-ray showing osseous hypertrophy and phalangeal enlargement
MRI demonstrating soft tissue overgrowth and fatty infiltration
genetic: Somatic mutations in PIK3CA gene reported in some cases
other: Clinical observation of progressive digit enlargement
Histopathology showing increased fibrofatty tissue proliferation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of cerebriform connective tissue nevi
Systemic manifestations absent in isolated macrodactyly
Limb hypertrophy involving entire extremity rather than isolated digits

redFlags: Rapid progression of digit enlargement beyond early childhood
Signs of neurovascular compromise in affected digit
Presence of systemic symptoms suggesting syndromic overgrowth
references: Al-Qattan MM. Macrodactyly: a review of 33 patients. J Hand Surg Am. 2001;26(4):655-661.
Lindhurst MJ, et al. A mosaic activating mutation in AKT1 associated with the Proteus syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2011;365(7):611-619.
